We have a small AC that can't cool our whole apartment that well so we're wondering if cracking a couple of top window sashes an inch will help get the hot air out until the rooms cool enough.

We'd only have the windows open for about 10 minutes.

Cold air sinks, hot air rises so wouldn't that hasten the cooling process?
Is it stupid to crack the top window sash while the AC is on to let hot air escape?
I follow this very same concept in my vehicle and it seems to help especially if I open the rear windows a bit.

If you're using the "AC MAX" setting, you're not helping. You,re wasting can and energy.

Your standard AC setting will pull air in from the outside, through the "gills" that are at the base of your front windshield, cool that air, and push it into your cab. Opening your window may help to cool you down faster, but I'm not sure.

But, using the "MAX AC" setting doesn't pull outside air in through these gills. It recycles the air that's already in your cab through the AC compressor, and puts it back in the cab. So, opening your window here will cause hot air to come in and mix with the air you're trying to cool, negating the work your AC compressor is doing. You're just letting the cooled air out, and hot air in.
You should only open the window furthest from the air conditioner. And make sure to close it promptly or else you will kill the AC motor.
